scenario: Two paths probed in one fixture: a tmpfs mount with usrquota (quota_state enabled) and an nfs4 mount (quota_state unknown, unsupported_fstype); the enabled path must win the run verdict (exit 1 QUOTA_ENABLED) while the unknown path is still reported as unknown.

rationale: Pre-seal amendment (round-23/preseal-amendment.md) supersedes only erroneous or ambiguous original clauses; this corrected case re-derives the same scenario under those superseding rules, with the original proposal left untouched in cases-proposed/. Contract section C2 (frozen at lane commit 4dc80c1be48308075e83af17f15fbfe7e95e6cb8) plus the amendment's C2 final rules, and the kernel sources S082/S084; no candidate implementation, oracle, or sibling expectation was read. DELTA FROM THE ORIGINAL PROPOSAL: exactly one change - the single btrfs_sysfs UUID record gains the required member qgroups_enabled, set to null because the record has qgroups=false (amendment: 'qgroups false must pair with enabled=null/mode=null'; qgroups fields must have exact bool/bool-or-null/mode-or-null types; missing or extra record keys are a setup error). No other fixture member and no expected value changes, and the amendment's other corrections (ext2/3/4 always unknown with basis ext_quota_option_unverified, duplicated covering mountpoint -> unknown/n/a/ambiguous_overmount with fstype=null and mount_point=null, enabled btrfs basis renamed btrfs_qgroups_enabled) do not touch this case: no probed path is an ext filesystem, no mount point in the fixture occurs twice, and no probed path resolves to the btrfs mount, so the btrfs basis token is never asserted here. Fixture schema per contract C2 and the amendment's fixture rules: exactly the keys schema, mountinfo, paths, device_links, btrfs_sysfs; the btrfs_sysfs record carries exactly devices, qgroups, qgroups_enabled, qgroups_mode; paths are nonempty, unique, normalized absolute path/realpath with no dot or dotdot components; st_dev values are canonical decimal MAJ:MIN (0:57, 0:82) with no signs and no leading zeros; the UUID key is a canonical UUID; devices and mapped device_links values are plain nonempty basenames without slashes or control characters. Mount resolution per contract C2 and the amendment: empty trailing lines are ignored (the mountinfo text ends with a newline, which therefore contributes no eighth line), the separator and the last three fields of each chosen line are parsed per line rather than file-wide, the longest component-prefix mount point wins, and no covering mount point occurs more than once in this fixture, so the ambiguous_overmount refusal does not apply; for realpath /srv/quota/data the candidates are the btrfs root mount '/' and the tmpfs mount '/srv/quota', and '/srv/quota' is longer and is chosen; for realpath /mnt/nfs4/data the candidates are '/' and '/mnt/nfs4', and '/mnt/nfs4' is longer and is chosen. The proc, sysfs, devtmpfs and btrfs lines are inert for these two paths but keep the mountinfo text structurally realistic. Device check per contract C2 and the amendment (device mismatch preempts the filesystem table; btrfs skips equality only when the stat major is 0): both chosen fstypes are non-btrfs, so the equality check is live, and each fixture path's st_dev is set equal to its chosen mount's major:minor (0:57 for tmpfs, 0:82 for nfs4), so neither path takes the device_mismatch branch and both reach the classification table; that equality is the normal non-btrfs situation because the kernel prints the superblock device in the mountinfo major:minor field (fs/proc_namespace.c show_mountinfo prints MAJOR(sb->s_dev), MINOR(sb->s_dev)) and a file on that filesystem reports the same st_dev. Path 1 classification - tmpfs: the contract's tmpfs row (any of quota,usrquota,grpquota or a key ending _hardlimit -> enabled, enforced, tmpfs_quota_option) applies because the tmpfs line's last field carries the key usrquota; the amendment narrows the hardlimit vocabulary to the four documented usrquota_block_hardlimit/usrquota_inode_hardlimit/grpquota_block_hardlimit/grpquota_inode_hardlimit keys and requires that 'enforced' describe mechanism flags rather than a nonzero limit, both of which are satisfied here because usrquota is itself a mechanism flag, so quota_state enabled, enforcement enforced, basis tmpfs_quota_option stand. Kernel anchor S084 (Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst v7.2, quota mount-option table lines 129-143): usrquota = 'User quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', quota = 'User and group quota accounting and enforcement is enabled on the mount', grpquota = the group equivalent, and the four *_hardlimit options set global limits; the kernel emits these flags into the mountinfo super-options field through the tmpfs show_options callback (mm/shmem.c shmem_show_options prints ',usrquota' when sb_has_quota_active(sb, USRQUOTA) is true, ',grpquota' likewise, then the *_hardlimit=<bytes> entries), so 'usrquota' in the last field is realistic; the contract and the amendment parse keys only, so option values are immaterial and are never emitted. Path 2 classification - nfs4: nfs4 is not xfs, btrfs, ext2/ext3/ext4 or tmpfs, so the table's final row applies (other -> unknown, n/a, unsupported_fstype); the nfs4 super options contain no quota key, the amendment records quota_option_keys=[] for unsupported fstypes, and the contract's limits state 'no NFS/server-side or overlay/fuse quota', so the probe must not infer a server-side quota state; expected quota_state unknown, enforcement n/a, basis unsupported_fstype. Verdict precedence per contract C2 and the amendment (setup error -> 2 QUOTA_SETUP; else any enabled -> 1 QUOTA_ENABLED, positive evidence is never hidden by an unknown sibling; else any unknown -> 2 QUOTA_STATE_UNKNOWN; else 0 QUOTA_DISABLED): there is no setup error - the fixture is well formed, in particular every btrfs_sysfs record now carries qgroups_enabled - and one path is enabled, so the run verdict is exit 1 with finding_id QUOTA_ENABLED; the unknown nfs4 sibling does not downgrade the verdict and is still reported with its own unknown state, which is exactly the anti-suppression check this case exists for. Source anchors relied on: S082 (Documentation/filesystems/proc.rst v7.2 section 3.5, lines 1965-1990 - field layout (1)..(6), optional tagged fields until the '-' separator, then (m+2) filesystem type, (m+3) mount source, (m+4) super options; 'Parsers should ignore all unrecognised optional fields') and S084 (Documentation/filesystems/tmpfs.rst v7.2 quota mount-option table, lines 129-143). Corroborating code opened read-only for realism only and not S-numbered in this round: fs/proc_namespace.c (show_mountinfo, show_sb_opts, seq_path_root with the ' \t\n\\' escape set) and mm/shmem.c (shmem_show_options).
